params.name: w_syn
params.note: published 0.275 (fitted there, against a female connectome); our earlier fit 0.075

params.name: inh_gain
params.note: inhibition relative to excitation per synapse; balanced-network models commonly use 4-8

params.name: tau_syn
params.note: published 5 ms; ionotropic GABA and GABA-B differ by 10-100x, which one constant cannot represent

params.name: v_th
params.note: published threshold sits 7 mV above rest

params.name: sigma
params.note: background noise. Ours, not the published model's, which has none -- so it is fitted rather than assumed

params.name: tau_mem
params.note: published 20 ms, applied to every cell

params.name: delay_ms
params.note: the published 1.8 ms is one number for every connection, but measured giant-fibre latencies are 0.93-1.46 ms across one synapse and 1.44-1.85 ms across two, so a hop costs far less than the base. Bounded by those measurements

params.name: tau_mem_kc
params.note: Kenyon cells are measured at >200 ms, a lower bound. Searched below it too, so the fit can disagree with the measurement visibly rather than silently

targets.note: 6 +- 5% of KCs respond to an odour, n=71, electrophysiology, 3.5 SD threshold. T-MB-17 says explicitly: loose tolerance.
blocking APL raises KC odour response and reduces sparseness. A direction, which a global rescaling cannot produce.
APL does not fire action potentials. Our spiking APL should at least not run hot; a graded APL would satisfy this exactly.
Kenyon cells are close to silent at baseline, by circuit design.
Rmax fitted per glomerulus: 170, 167, 163, 144 spikes/s. Tolerance spans the spread plus room for our different drive.

a substantial population of antennal lobe local interneurons does not spike at all; the fraction is not quantified. Held out because our 227 Hz is so far off that fitting to it would dominate everything else.
projection neurons rest close to spike threshold. No published number exists in fluctuation widths, so this encodes 'close' loosely and is held out rather than fitted.
no brain-wide rate distribution has ever been measured, so this is not a measurement -- it encodes only that a brain in which four cells in five never fire is not a plausible resting state.
not from a paper: the order of magnitude implied by the per-cell-type recordings we do have. Marked internal so it is never cited as measured.
